title: Reinstate a conditional vehicle registration
summary: Find out what to do if your conditional vehicle registration is cancelled or has lapsed, and how to reinstate it.
intro:
If you've been told that your conditional registration will soon be (or has been) cancelled, and you believe this to be incorrect, you'll need to take the vehicle with the plate(s) attached, to a Service NSW Centre.

If the registration has lapsed, or was cancelled because the vehicle was sold, you'll need to apply for a new conditional registration.
who_can_apply: You must take the vehicle with the plate(s) attached to a Service NSW Centre if you believe your conditional registration cancellation is incorrect.
You must apply for a new conditional registration if the existing registration has lapsed or was cancelled because the vehicle was sold.
what_you_need: The vehicle with the plates intact
Documents proving that the registration should be reinstated
The refund cheque if it was sent

faqs.q: What should I do if my conditional registration is cancelled?
faqs.a: If you believe your conditional registration cancellation is incorrect, take the vehicle with the plate(s) attached to a Service NSW Centre.

faqs.q: What if my registration has lapsed or the vehicle was sold?
faqs.a: If the registration has lapsed, or was cancelled because the vehicle was sold, you will need to apply for a new conditional registration.
